tagline: Modifies filter context — the most important DAX function

slides.title: What CALCULATE Does
slides.body: CALCULATE evaluates an expression inside a modified filter context. It is the only DAX function that can change which filters are active during an evaluation.
slides.keyPoint: CALCULATE(Expression, Filter1, Filter2, ...) — each filter argument replaces existing context for that column.

slides.title: Starting Data — Sales Table
slides.caption: All four rows are visible before any filter is applied

slides.title: The Expression
slides.code:
Bike Sales North =
CALCULATE(
    SUM(Sales[Amount]),
    Sales[Product] = "Bike",
    Sales[Region] = "North"
)
slides.annotation: Two filter arguments use AND logic. CALCULATE replaces the existing filter context with these constraints before evaluating SUM.

slides.title: Filters Applied
slides.caption: CALCULATE keeps only rows satisfying ALL filter arguments

slides.title: Final Result
slides.unit: SUM of Amount where Product = Bike AND Region = North

slides.title: Key Rules to Remember
bullets: Multiple filter arguments use AND logic — all conditions must be satisfied
A filter on the same column REPLACES (not adds to) the existing context for that column
CALCULATE is required to use time intelligence functions like SAMEPERIODLASTYEAR
ALL() or REMOVEFILTERS() inside CALCULATE removes an existing filter rather than adding one
slides.warning: CALCULATE does NOT automatically ignore slicers. It modifies context — to ignore slicers, you must explicitly use ALL() or REMOVEFILTERS() on the relevant columns.
